neighbours.label: A handicap on how a task must be done: fires on the word that introduces the restriction ("without ...", "using only ...", "limited to ...", "in a single ..."); output promotes ' constrained', ' limited', ' restricted'
fire: The puzzle asks you to connect all nine dots without lifting your pen from the paper.
In the final round, the bakers must decorate the cake using only one hand.
Under the new rules, each climber is restricted to a single rope for the whole ascent.
Your task is to move the tower to the third peg in no more than seven moves.
The sailors had to cross the bay without using the engine or the radio.
For this exercise, describe your home town in exactly ten words, no more!
Players have to get the ball into the basket while keeping one foot on the line.
Space on the boat was tight, so every passenger was limited to one small bag.
quiet: The puzzle shows nine dots on a sheet of paper, and children enjoy colouring them.
In the final round, the bakers decorated the cake and presented it to the crowd.
After the new season opened, each climber brought a rope for the whole ascent.
Your friend moved the tower to the third peg and then went home for lunch.
The sailors crossed the bay in the morning and tied up near the old pier.
For this exercise, she described her home town and showed us some photographs.
Players got the ball into the basket many times and the fans cheered loudly.
The boat was large and bright, and every passenger carried a small bag aboard.

notes: Card: top examples are 'restricted to a single shot', 'without breaking any', 'You cannot use your hands!', 'in a single bound'. Probes: four restriction sentences 0.36-0.68, two unrestricted versions 0.00-0.01.
